item.title: The Emotional Reality Bender
item.description: A reality bender who can only affect a certain amount of objects at a time depending on her mood.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
This SCP was born as an reality bender also known as a type green. Unlike most type greens she is rather limited with her ability's seemingly only being able to affect a few things at an time depending on her mood. When she is sad she can't affect anything and when she's angry or scared she can affect many things. Although how she can affect these objects is not limited.

Central Narrative:
Within the article it will talk about a policy on how staff should treat the SCP such as how they should talk down to her and to try to keep her in a sad mood pretty much. This and a combination of test some being somewhat cruel (Researchers doing test without permission) will make her unstable emotionally which may lead to her becoming more dangerous.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I'm hoping to hook the reader with a series of interviews and tests within the article. I also hope that the reader gets invested with the SCP it's self and to perhaps even feel bad for her or to think that the things done to keep her sad is for the best.

Additional Notes:
If this does get greenlighted this would be my first SCP so this will be a learning experience for me so I will try my hardest to make a fun and interesting SCP. If everything goes well I may make a tale around her potential termination because of how dangerous she has become after becoming unstable.

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantom/The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: An SCP heavily and very directly inspired by Christine, The Wraith, Death Proof and SLR:Redline.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a 1970 Chevrolet Camaro that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer encounters the SCP and the road transitions into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with the stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others have reported the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car as it appears and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins. At one point, a GoI will have blown the car up (no clue, which one, yet), after which, basically, Christine happens: Someone finds a junker 1970 Camaro, and with maniacal passion, restores it, builds it and crashes it violently - thus causing the phantom to be "reborn". From then on, the Foundation tries to relocate it to the most deserted stretch of blacktop possible and keep it happy by regularly setting up drag races.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, where does the car come from, is anyone behind the wheel, how can it be contained etc. etc. The origins part only really comes in only before the SCP is "reborn", after which all focus is on active study and containment - origin study is moved to a passive state.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that flat-out disables digital devices (not electronic)./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they race or crash, at which point they become part of the SCP./The phantom sustains itself off of life energy gained in the final stage of its "rebirth"./It is sentient and has a memory./It can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

P.S. Apologies to everyone who got my email with no subject, I was very concentrated on outreach first

item.title: [Need Greenlight] The bipolar statue
item.description: Also, has this been done before?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Elevator Pitch:A simple bronze statue, 3 meters in height, with an emotionless, nondescript face. The statue, each day of the year, produces an object that is laid at the feet of the statue. This object can vary, from a blank book, a briefcase of money, or a gun. The way this object is used depends on the weather, therefore creating an infinite amount of possibilities for what could happen, with global warming and greenhouse gases. The statue also sometimes goes into a "bad" mood, with the item that is produced being used against the person picking it up, for example, a handgun produced at the feet of the statue could have the safety off and be fully loaded, giving a chance for the person picking it up to shoot themselves if they are not careful.
Central Narrative: Not sure what they are talking about, so… none?
Hook/attention grabber: Its a statue that can give you a "gift" or kill you.

item.title: The Friendly Shadow
item.description: Clarence's Shadow is alive, sentient, and his best friend.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A sentient, living shadow, who belongs to a man named Clarence.

+ The Friendly Shadow's Quirk Ideas
- Close

Whether these are a good ideas or not is why I'm putting these here. Yell out if any seem good or bad. I always like to hear feedback and opinions.

  1. I was thinking that the shadow could move off of Clarence and interact with other shadows of people and objects. When the shadow interacts with any other shadow, object or person, he can move it as he can interact with it just like any other person could with psychical objects. If he picks up the shadow of a remote, it will float above the spot he is holding it. If he pats someone's shadow on the back, the physical person will feel the same effect. He can do this off and on Clarence.
  2. The shadow can only talk to people through charades. It doesn't have a physical mouth, so it can't talk.

Central Narrative: It revolves around the wholesome relationship between Clarence and his Shadow.

+ Expanding on the Narrative
- Close

I'm hoping to let this be emotional. I want a rather wholesome attachment with Clarence and his shadow. They have known of each other since childhood. It's not some recent anomaly. They've been best friends for life, sharing each other accomplishments, laughing together, and working together. Even if Shadow's accomplishments are more private and hidden to onlookers.
The big twist is that Clarence is created by the shadow. This being why it's not some recent anomaly and why the Foundation can't find any link to Clarence's family. This will be unfolded in the Addendum.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Clarence was made by the Shadow. As a friend and a mobile person to keep attached too and see the world.

Additional Notes:

+ The Inspiration
- Close

For those who are as nerdy as me, the inspiration behind this was three things specifically.

  1. The Movie which has yet to (or may never) be released, Me and My Shadow. Note: If you've seen or are about to look up what this is, you'll know this had the biggest impact of the three.
  2. Peter Pan and his shadow
  3. Doctor Who, Season 4, Episode 8, Silence in the Library.

Let me know what can be used (if anything can be). Can't wait to hear from you. -Cope

Thanks Blazer. - Cope

item.title: The Mushroom Men
item.description: A sentient and talented species of fungus and the funerary cave in their charge, their lifestyle, history, territory, uses and peril...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tribe of sentient fungus people clawing out a living on the edge of the Lake Bikal Secure Containment Zone…

  • See the funerary cave they maintain and a peculiar stone age corpse within, deformed from a long, losing battle against SCP 610. (I do have a mystery for this in mind, but i'm not spoiling it.)
  • Hear of their mycelial network, like a brain unto itself in complexity, capable of healing, administering medications and poisons, and communicating directly with the land itself.
  • Their reproduction is slowed by climate change drying out the soil they live in and leaching it of nutrients. The permafrost is melting, the warm temperatures and drier weather are slowly killing them. If the Foundation doesn't take drastic measures to preserve them they'll go extinct in less than a century. Worse, its believed they keep the terraforming effects of SCP 610 in check. Without them, future 610 breaches will probably cause much more damage.

*I'm working on an ongoing connected series of articles and a story shared between them with conservation being the underlying thread. This is part of that.

Central Narrative: A more ecologically based view of the OG Sarkic Anomaly, the amazing environmental flexibility of fungi and their age old conflict with bacteria, musings of what a sentient mushroom might look like, and whether there really is a separation between flesh, nature, and machine.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Loosely inspired by a cave painting and the work of Professor Paul Stamets. I tried to capture the uses and habits of fungi and their importance to the environment in an SCP, from the best known to the theoretical. They also pose a different kind of breach risk to the Foundation, one I attempted to base on real life concerns over the human consequences of climate change.

Additional Notes: OMG I did it! A proposal that expresses everything I wanted to in less than 400 words!!!!!
